audit.whatIsWrong: The chart on this page reads Skill/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Gnar/Gnar in both layers, while the packet and the already-published mirror both read Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Lillia.
audit.why: The content why-strings already argue the packet chart word for word — whys[2] literally opens 'Even now', whys[5] ends 'call it even', whys[6] is a clean Lillia win. Only the enum rows and the full-layer why text lagged. Leaving it means this page and the Gnar page answer 'who wins 2+ items' differently.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Lillia in both layers, with ratings moved to match (Level 1 to 3/10, 2+ items to 7/10 — the inverse of the mirror's 3/10).

audit.whatIsWrong: No spike carries a real number, and dosFull[2].d treats GNAR! as a thing he 'spends early' with no cooldown given.
audit.why: GNAR! is 90/60/30 — 90 seconds at rank 1, an enormous window. Wallop is 7s flat. Boomerang Throw is 16s at rank 1 but refunds on catch. Lilting Lullaby costs 150s at rank 1. Those are the numbers that turn 'bait it' into a plan.
audit.corrected: 90s on GNAR!, 7s on Wallop, 150s on Lilting Lullaby, and the 1100-vs-450 range gap written into the early/mid/late text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings credit 'GNAR!' with an AoE stun that locks Lillia mid-kite. That is Wallop, Mega Gnar's W.
audit.why: Riot's text: Mega Gnar's W 'can rear up on his hind legs and smash down on the area in front of him, stunning enemies in an area' — 7 second cooldown, available constantly in Mega form. GNAR! (R) throws enemies in a direction and stuns ONLY those thrown into a wall, on 90s at rank 1. Telling a Lillia player to fear a 90-second ultimate when the actual lane threat is a 7-second W makes her mis-time every trade in Mega form.
audit.corrected: Wallop named as the 7s area stun and the real lockdown; GNAR! restricted to its wall condition and its 90s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Lilting Lullaby is described as if it can sleep Gnar on demand.
audit.why: Riot's text: it causes 'all enemies with Dream Dust on them' to become Drowsy. Without a prior Q or E landing, the ultimate does nothing at all — the mirror recorded the same precondition. This is the difference between a 150-second game-winner and a 150-second whiff.
audit.corrected: The Dream Dust precondition written into spikes[2].text, whys[4] and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'my hop range', 'close the gap diagonally', 'jog through it' all imply Lillia has mobility she does not have.
audit.why: Blooming Blows is a 450-range point-blank AoE with stacking move speed; Watch Out! Eep! is 500-range point-blank. She has no dash, so she must WALK into Gnar's range to do anything — which is the whole reason the 1100-range Boomerang Throw wins the early stages.
audit.corrected: 'hop range' replaced with the real 450 Q radius; 'you have no dash' stated in early.

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid and late are written in FIRST PERSON ('me', 'I', 'my') throughout.
audit.why: The rest of the site is in the user's second-person coaching voice. First-person breaks it on three of the longest strings on the page.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten in second person at the same length.

audit.whatIsWrong: Swirlseed's terrain flag is a tooltip-parsing artefact.
audit.why: Riot's text says the seed rolls until it hits a wall or target — it does not create terrain. Not written in.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 belong to Gnar — mini-Gnar's Boomerang Throw and his longer auto range out-poke me while I only have Blooming Blows and no movement-speed chain yet to close on him. Don't throw a Q sweetspot I can't reach him with; just farm at range and eat as little boomerang as possible. The Dream Dust passive only matters once I can land Q and E to apply it, so I'm conceding the opener and waiting for my kite stacks to come online rather than walking into his chip on a squishy body.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 belong to Gnar — mini-Gnar's Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 units and his auto range out-pokes you while you have only Blooming Blows at 450 and no move-speed stacks yet. You have no dash: every Q is point-blank, so don't walk in for a sweetspot you can't survive. Farm at range and eat as little boomerang as possible. Dream Dust only starts once a Q or E lands, so concede the opener and wait for your kite stacks rather than feeding chip on a squishy body.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 even it out and are my best lane stretch — full-rank Blooming Blows plus the Dream Dust burn from a Swirlseed slow lets me chip every time he steps up, and the stacking Q move speed makes mini-Gnar's kite far harder to maintain. Land E to slow him into my hop range, then layer Q sweetspots so the DoT compounds. The thing to dodge is his Rage bar: a mega transform with the GNAR! AOE stun locks me mid-kite for his whole combo, so trade hard while he's mini and back off the instant he's near full Rage. At 6 my Lilting Lullaby is a real but situational answer — best saved to punish a mega-Gnar who just whiffed or spent his stun.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 even it out and are your best lane stretch — full-rank Blooming Blows plus the Dream Dust burn off a Swirlseed slow chips him on every step-up, and stacking Q move speed makes mini-Gnar's kite hard to hold. Land the 700-range E to slow him into your 450 Q, then layer sweetspots so the DoT compounds. Watch his Rage bar: a Mega transform brings Wallop, a 7-second area stun that pins you mid-kite for his whole combo, so trade hard while he is mini and back off the instant he nears full Rage. At 6 Lilting Lullaby is real but situational — it costs 150 seconds and only sleeps targets already carrying Dream Dust.

edits.before: This is where I take over. Once Liandry's or Riftmaker comes online, my W slam and the Dream Dust DoT start dealing serious percent-HP damage, and that out-skirmishes Gnar's fixed boomerang chip in any extended fight — his poke is flat while my burn scales with his health bar. The stacking Q move speed plus my passive means I'm permanently out of reach in a kite war he can't win without landing mega GNAR!. Keep dodging that one stun, isolate-sleep him or a teammate with R, and convert this into roams and skirmishes before the game drags long enough for true hyperscalers to matter.
edits.after: This is where you take over. Once Liandry's or Riftmaker lands, Watch Out! Eep! and the Dream Dust DoT deal serious percent-HP damage, and that out-skirmishes Gnar's fixed Boomerang Throw in any extended fight — his poke is flat while your burn scales with his health bar. Stacking Q move speed keeps you out of reach in a kite war he cannot win without landing Wallop, or pinning you on a wall with GNAR! at 90 seconds a cast. Dodge those two, mark a target with Dream Dust before you press R, and convert into roams and skirmishes before hyperscalers matter.

notes: Chart rows proposed as one atomic group, every phases[N].side paired with its win[N]. Stages 2, 4 and 5 already matched the packet and are untouched. I left diff/diffRating at EVEN 5.5/10: the packet's 60% win rate rests on only 5 games, and the corrected chart (two Gnar stages, four even, one Lillia) reads as an even lane. The biggest correction here is Wallop vs GNAR! — six strings called the ultimate the lane's stun when the actual 7-second area stun is Mega Gnar's W.
